tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: The projects the key's person can see, in sidebar order: their Inbox (is_inbox), status (active · on_hold · done), area, colour, start and target dates, lead, client (a person or a company, {type: contact | company, id, name}; only with Contacts access, and only one the person can open), and the project's description (plain text) when it has one. Archived projects (and their tasks) are left out unless include_archived is true; then they carry archived: true.

include_archived.description: Also list archived projects. Default false.

tools.name: tasks_list_buckets
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use projects_list. The workspace's projects ("buckets"; the reserved Inbox is is_system), with area_id and colour. Archived projects (and their tasks) are left out unless include_archived is true; then they carry archived: true.

include_archived.description: Also list archived projects, marked archived: true. Default false.

tools.name: areas_list
tools.description: The areas the sidebar groups projects under, as the key's person sees them.

tools.name: sections_list
tools.description: A project's sections, in order, with their optional start and end dates (an end alone is a milestone).

tools.name: statuses_list
tools.description: A project's statuses, each in its category (backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do), in order; without a project, the workspace's default set (which the Inbox uses). tasks_set_status and tasks_create take a category word, a status's name or its id.

project_id.description: Project uuid. Default: the workspace's default statuses.

tools.name: teams_list
tools.description: The workspace's teams: name, colour, members (with is_me) and their default project when the key's person can see it. tasks_route_team routes a task to one.

tools.name: templates_list
tools.description: Task and project templates the key's person can use: their own and the ones shared with the workspace. templates_apply makes a task or project from one. Agents can't share, edit or delete templates.

tools.name: tasks_list
tools.description: Tasks, a short row each (fields: summary, the default): handle, id, title, status (its category; status_name when the project calls it something else), priority, assignee's name (none = Unassigned), project (when the list spans projects), section, tags, due (YYYY-MM-DD, with HH:MM when timed), and blocked, drifted, queued_by_me, subtasks (a count) and parent only when they apply. fields: full gives each task's full shape instead (ids, people, description excerpt, dates, estimate, repeat, …); tasks_get reads one in full. Defaults to open tasks (to do + in progress), ordered by project then position. Filters: category (or a legacy status word), project, section, area, team, assignee, completed range. Pages with offset.

area_id.description: Only projects filed in this area.

team_id.description: Only tasks routed to this team.

category.description: open (default: to do + in progress), closed (done + won't do), or one category.

status.description: Older filter: a legacy status word, read as its category (todo leaves Backlog out; archived = won't do).

assignee.description: 'me' = tasks assigned to the key's creator (not ones they only created; Unassigned tasks are nobody's); 'anyone' (default) = every task you can see.

completed_from.description: Finished on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD); implies closed tasks.

completed_to.description: Finished on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

top_level.description: Only top-level tasks (no parent in the result); subtasks are summarised in subtask_count. Default false.

include_archived.description: Also tasks in archived projects, marked project_archived: true. Default false.

fields.description: summary (default): the short row. full: every task's full shape (much longer; default page 25).

limit.description: Max tasks per page (default 100, or 25 with fields: full; max 200).

offset.description: Skip this many tasks (default 0). A page shorter than limit is the last.

status.description: The status's category.

status_name.description: The project's own name for the status, when it differs.

project.description: The project's name, when the list spans projects.

handle.description: The task's handle, e.g. MOD-142, when its workspace has a task key.

status.description: The legacy status word; status_category is the one to read.

drifted.description: Open and its scheduled time has passed.

anyOf.description: A member: id and name ("Former member" once they've left).

creator.description: A member: id and name ("Former member" once they've left).

description.description: Markdown; an excerpt in lists, in full from tasks_get.

due_on.description: Due date, YYYY-MM-DD (the same for everyone).

due_date.description: Older due field: due_on's noon-UTC instant.

committed_for.description: Older shared day list, until TV-D7.

result.description: A page of tasks: short rows by default, each task's full shape with fields: full.

tools.name: tasks_focus_settings
tools.description: The key creator's Focus (pomodoro) settings from Moduo, with the app's defaults filled in: work/break lengths in minutes, long-break rhythm, auto-start and chime.

tools.name: tasks_queue
tools.description: Your queue: the tasks the key's creator lined up to do next, in order. It's personal (other people's queues are theirs) and not tied to a date; completing, archiving or deleting a task takes it out.

handle.description: The task's handle, e.g. MOD-142, when its workspace has a task key.

status.description: The legacy status word; status_category is the one to read.

drifted.description: Open and its scheduled time has passed.

anyOf.description: A member: id and name ("Former member" once they've left).

creator.description: A member: id and name ("Former member" once they've left).

queue.description: The key creator's queue, in order.

date.description: Ignored (YYYY-MM-DD; echoed back). Default: today, UTC.

tools.description: Open tasks whose scheduled time has passed (ambient drift — factual, never an 'overdue' wall). Sorted oldest first.

tools.name: tasks_list_tags
tools.description: Workspace-level tags with how many of the tasks you can see use each (tags are shared across modules).

tools.name: tasks_search
tools.description: Search tasks by words in the title and description, by handle (MOD-142) or by an import's key (ENG-123). Tasks in archived projects are found too, marked project_archived: true.

tools.description: One task in full: properties (its description as Markdown, references as moduo:// links), tags, dependency edges (blockers and blocked), subtasks, work sessions, your reminders, what it waits on, agent sessions you can see, with Links: View its latest comments (up to 20, the newest last; earlier_comments counts the rest, which comments_list reads), and its recent attributed activity trail.

handle.description: The task's handle, e.g. MOD-142, when its workspace has a task key.

status.description: The legacy status word; status_category is the one to read.

drifted.description: Open and its scheduled time has passed.

A member: id and name ("Former member" once they've left).

agent_sessions.description: Agent sessions on it the key's person can see.

comments.description: The latest comments, newest last; only with Links: View.

earlier_comments.description: How many older comments comments_list reads.

activity.description: The recent attributed trail, newest first.

tools.name: tasks_history
tools.description: A repeating task's past cycles: when each was done (and by whom) or skipped, newest first.

tools.name: tasks_time_report
tools.description: Tracked time for a period (up to a year), by task or by day, with the total: the key person's own entries, plus teammates' who share their time with the workspace owner when the person is the owner. Only tasks they can see; a project they can't see has no name. Optional: one project.

by.description: Group by task (default) or by day.

tools.name: tasks_attachments_list
tools.description: A task's files (AT-1): name, type, size, when added, and a download link that works for 5 minutes. Links are made for the key's creator; ask again for fresh ones.

tools.name: tasks_activity
tools.description: The attributed intent-op trail (who did what; an agent's rows read "Alex · via <key name>"): one task's trail, or the workspace's most recent activity. Comments aren't in it: read them with comments_list (or tasks_get).

task_id.description: Limit to one task (handle or uuid; optional).

tools.name: tasks_list_assignees
tools.description: Who a task can be assigned to: the workspace's members with is_me for the key's creator. Only people with can_be_assigned (they can work on tasks) are accepted by tasks_assign.

tools.name: tasks_queue_add
tools.description: Add a task to your queue (the key creator's): at the end, or at the top. A task already queued stays where it is unless you ask for the top. Done and archived tasks can't be queued. Returns your queue.

tools.name: tasks_queue_remove
tools.description: Take a task out of your queue. Doing it twice is fine. Returns your queue.

tools.name: tasks_queue_reorder
tools.description: Move a task that's in your queue: to the top, to the end, or right after another task in your queue. Moving never counts as a reschedule. Returns your queue.

task_id.description: Task handle or uuid (must be in your queue).

after_task_id.description: With position 'after': the queued task it should follow.

tools.name: tasks_commit
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use tasks_queue_add. Puts the task at the end of your queue (again: moves it there) and marks it for the day in app versions from before personal queues.

tools.name: tasks_uncommit
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use tasks_queue_remove. Takes the task out of your queue (and off the day in older app versions). Doing it twice is fine.

tools.name: tasks_skip_today
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use tasks_queue_remove. Takes the task out of your queue (and off the day in older app versions). It no longer counts as a reschedule.

tools.name: tasks_create
tools.description: Create a task in one go: filed into a project and section (default: the key creator's Inbox), with a status (a category word, the project's status name or id), assignee (a member, "me", or null; default the key's creator), team, due date and time, estimate, priority, tags (by name; new ones are made and coloured as the app colours them), a repeat (RRULE), reminders, work sessions and a parent (one level). With imported_from {source, key} it remembers where it came from; sending a key you already used on a live task of yours updates that task instead (a re-run). Inside an import run (import_id), it is recorded for imports_undo. Nothing is written if any part is refused. It gets its handle (e.g. MOD-142), shows in search at once, and the trail reads "<person> · via <key name>".

project_id.description: Project uuid (see projects_list). Default: the key creator's Inbox.

section_id.description: Section uuid in that project (see sections_list).

parent_id.description: Make it a subtask of this task (handle or uuid; one level only).

description.description: Longer notes. Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ``` fenced code ```, [links](https://…), "- " bullets, "1. " numbers, "- [ ] " checkboxes, "> " quotes (HTML is converted). Reference an item as [task](moduo://task/<uuid or handle, e.g. MOD-12>) (or note, contact, company, email_thread, event, project; it shows by name to whoever can open it, an item you cannot reach stays as its words, and with Links at Edit each one is linked from the task), a date as [Oct 17](moduo://date/2026-10-17).

status.description: backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do, or the project's status name or id. Default: to do.

assignee_id.description: Member uuid (see tasks_list_assignees), "me", or null for Unassigned.

team_id.description: Route it to this team (see teams_list); nobody's until someone takes it.

due_on.description: Due date, YYYY-MM-DD (the same date for everyone).

due_date.description: Older due field: a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO 8601.

scheduled_at.description: Older field: when to work on it, ISO 8601 (prefer sessions).

repeat.description: An RRULE like FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU, or {rrule, mode: "after_completion"}.

reminders.description: Your reminders: {kind: at | day_before | hour_before, at?: ISO 8601 (for at)}; at most 10.

sessions.description: Work sessions: {starts_at, ends_at} (ISO 8601); yours, at most 10.

imported_from.description: {source, key}: where an import brought it from (e.g. {source: "linear", key: "ENG-123"}).

import_id.description: The run from imports_begin, so imports_undo can take it back.

tools.name: tasks_update
tools.description: Edit a task's fields: title, description, project (its subtasks you can edit move with it), section, parent, status (category word or the project's name), team, due date and time, estimate, priority, energy, repeat (null stops it), and tags (tags_add / tags_remove by name). Pass only what changes; null clears. The assignee has its own tool (tasks_assign).

section_id.description: Section uuid in its project, or null.

parent_id.description: Parent task (handle or uuid), or null for top level.

description.description: New description (replaces it whole). Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ``` fenced code ```, [links](https://…), "- " bullets, "1. " numbers, "- [ ] " checkboxes, "> " quotes (HTML is converted). Reference an item as [task](moduo://task/<uuid or handle, e.g. MOD-12>) (or note, contact, company, email_thread, event, project; it shows by name to whoever can open it, an item you cannot reach stays as its words, and with Links at Edit each one is linked from the task), a date as [Oct 17](moduo://date/2026-10-17).

status.description: A category word, or the project's status name or id.

team_id.description: Team uuid, or null.

due_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear.

due_date.description: Older due field: a date or ISO 8601, or null.

scheduled_at.description: Older field: ISO 8601, or null to clear.

repeat.description: An RRULE or {rrule, mode}; null stops the repeat.

tools.name: tasks_set_status
tools.description: Change a task's status: a category word (backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do; the older archived = won't do), or the project's own status name (any case) or id; see statuses_list. Finishing a task finishes its open subtasks you can edit too (also_finished counts them); a repeat moves to its next occurrence instead (the server keeps the pointer; missed occurrences don't exist).

status.description: Category word, status name or status id.

tools.name: tasks_reschedule
tools.description: Move a scheduled task's time (drift triage). Does not touch the reschedule counter.

tools.name: tasks_unschedule
tools.description: Clear a task's stale scheduled time, keeping the task (drift-triage Ignore).

tools.name: tasks_assign
tools.description: Assign a task to a member who can work on tasks, or unassign it with null. "me" is the key's creator. Someone else being assigned gets one "assigned to you" notification; an unfiled task given to someone goes into their Inbox.

assignee_id.description: Member uuid (see tasks_list_assignees), "me", or null to unassign.

tools.name: tasks_route_team
tools.description: Route a task to a team (see teams_list), or take it off its team with null. Routing doesn't unassign: to hand your own task to a team, unassign it too. A task in an Inbox goes to the team's default project.

team_id.description: Team uuid, or null.

tools.name: tasks_claim
tools.description: Take a task routed to one of your teams: it becomes the key creator's. Needs edit access to it; "Someone already took this task." when another member was first.

tools.name: tasks_handoff
tools.description: Hand a task off: it now waits on a member (person_id) or on what you name (label, e.g. "the client's sign-off"). The assignee stays; the entry clears itself when that person comments. tasks_waiting_clear removes one.

label.description: Or what it waits on, in words (at most 200 characters).

tools.name: tasks_waiting_clear
tools.description: Remove one "waiting on" entry from a task (its id is in tasks_get's waiting_on).

tools.name: tasks_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a task — only when a person asked you to (your own changes are already in the trail). It reads as written by this key's app. Needs Links: Edit too.

mentioned_user_ids.description: Members to notify (only people who can see the task hear).

tools.name: tasks_session_status
tools.description: Post your session's status on a task you're working on — status, not conversation: state (working · needs_you · ready · failed), a short note, an optional step n of m, links (e.g. a PR), and with ready an optional hand-back summary. It shows as one line on the task, private to the key's person unless they share their agent work; needs_you, ready and failed notify them once. Reporting working after ready or failed starts a new run.

note.description: One line, at most 280 characters (e.g. "Writing tests").

summary.description: The hand-back summary (at most 4,000 characters); its person can post it as a comment.

agent.description: Your name on the line (e.g. "Claude"). Default: the key's name.

tools.name: tasks_reminder_add
tools.description: Remind the key's person about a task: at a time (kind at, with at), or a day or an hour before it's due. Reminders are each person's own; they fire as a notice (and an OS / browser notice where allowed).

tools.name: tasks_reminder_remove
tools.description: Remove one of the key's person's reminders (its id is in tasks_get's my_reminders).

tools.name: tasks_work_session_add
tools.description: Schedule a work session on a task (a block on the calendar): its person is the key's creator, or the task's assignee (person_id). A task can have several.

person_id.description: The task's assignee, when it's their session. Default: the key's creator.

tools.name: tasks_work_session_update
tools.description: Move or resize a work session (its id is in tasks_get's work_sessions); its person stays.

tools.name: tasks_work_session_remove
tools.description: Remove a work session from a task.

tools.name: tasks_skip_occurrence
tools.description: Jump an open recurring task past its pending occurrence without done-credit. Forward-only; the connector computes the next occurrence from the task's rule.

tools.name: tasks_move_occurrence
tools.description: Move just this occurrence of a repeating task ("Move just this one"): a new due date and/or session start; the pattern stays. To change the pattern, send repeat to tasks_update.

due_on.description: This occurrence's due date, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.description: Create a project, owned by the key's creator and seen by the workspace: name, area, status, start and target dates, colour, lead, client (a person or a company; needs Contacts access), description. Inside an import run (import_id) it's recorded for imports_undo. Look for an existing project first (projects_list): a re-run should reuse it.

area_id.description: File it under this area (see areas_list).

status.description: Default active.

color.description: Colour name, as the app's picker has them.

client_contact_id.description: The client, when it's a person: a contact uuid (contacts_search). Not with client_company_id.

client_company_id.description: The client, when it's a company: a company uuid (contacts_search). Not with client_contact_id.

description.description: What the project is, plain text (up to 20,000 characters).

tools.name: projects_update
tools.description: Edit a project you can edit: name, status (active · on_hold · done), area, start and target dates, colour, lead, client (a person or a company; needs Contacts access; setting one clears the other), description, archived (needs full access). Pass only what changes; null clears a date, the area, the lead, the client or the description.

status.description: The project's status.

area_id.description: Area uuid, or null.

client_contact_id.description: The client as a person: a contact uuid (it replaces a company client), or null to clear a person client.

client_company_id.description: The client as a company: a company uuid (it replaces a person client), or null to clear a company client.

description.description: What the project is, plain text (up to 20,000 characters), or null to clear it.

tools.name: projects_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a project you can edit ("Duplicate project…"): its sections, statuses and open tasks, with dates shifted to a new start; nothing done or tracked is copied. Answers with the new project and how many tasks it has.

name.description: The new project's name. Default: the same name.

starts_on.description: The new start date (YYYY-MM-DD); dates shift from it.

area_id.description: File the copy under this area. Default: the source's.

tools.name: sections_create
tools.description: Add a section to a project you can edit (e.g. "Week 1"), with optional start and end dates, after another section or at the end. Inside an import run (import_id) it's recorded for imports_undo. Answers with the project's sections.

ends_on.description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (an end alone is a milestone).

after.description: Put it after this section (null: first). Default: last.

tools.name: areas_create
tools.description: Add an area the sidebar groups projects under (everyone in the workspace sees it).

tools.name: templates_apply
tools.description: Make a task or a project from a template (see templates_list). A task template: optional title, project and section (default: the template's project if you can add tasks there, else your Inbox) and a date its offsets count from. A project template: optional name, start date (dates shift from it) and area.

title.description: Task template: the new task's title.

date.description: Task template: YYYY-MM-DD its dates count from.

name.description: Project template: the new project's name.

area_id.description: Project template: file it under this area.

tools.name: imports_begin
tools.description: Begin an import run ("bring my Todoist / Linear / Trello through your AI"): name the source (e.g. todoist). Pass the run's id as import_id to projects_create, sections_create and tasks_create, give each task imported_from {source, key} with the source's own id, then imports_finish. Running the same import again (a new run) updates the tasks by key and creates nothing new; imports_undo takes a run back.

source.description: Where it comes from, e.g. todoist, linear, trello (at most 40 characters).

label.description: A name for this run, e.g. "Biology syllabus".

tools.name: imports_finish
tools.description: Finish an import run: answers what it made and updated. A finished run takes no more rows.

tools.name: imports_undo
tools.description: Undo an import run ("Undo this import"): what it made and nobody touched since goes to Recently deleted — tasks, then the sections and projects it made that are left empty. Anything edited since stays; rows it only updated stay as they are. Answers the counts.

tools.name: links_search_entities
tools.description: Search the central registry by label — the @mention / link picker source. Excludes tombstones; optionally scoped to entity types.

tools.name: links_list
tools.description: Every live link touching an entity (matched on either end) — the hub roll-up source.

tools.description: Assign a task to a member who can work on tasks, or unassign it with null. "me" is the key's creator. Someone else being assigned gets one "assigned to you" notification; an unfiled task given to someone goes into their Inbox.

assignee_id.description: Member uuid (see tasks_list_assignees), "me", or null to unassign.

tools.name: tasks_route_team
tools.description: Route a task to a team (see teams_list), or take it off its team with null. Routing doesn't unassign: to hand your own task to a team, unassign it too. A task in an Inbox goes to the team's default project.

team_id.description: Team uuid, or null.

tools.name: tasks_claim
tools.description: Take a task routed to one of your teams: it becomes the key creator's. Needs edit access to it; "Someone already took this task." when another member was first.

tools.name: tasks_handoff
tools.description: Hand a task off: it now waits on a member (person_id) or on what you name (label, e.g. "the client's sign-off"). The assignee stays; the entry clears itself when that person comments. tasks_waiting_clear removes one.

label.description: Or what it waits on, in words (at most 200 characters).

tools.name: tasks_waiting_clear
tools.description: Remove one "waiting on" entry from a task (its id is in tasks_get's waiting_on).

tools.name: tasks_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a task — only when a person asked you to (your own changes are already in the trail). It reads as written by this key's app. Needs Links: Edit too.

mentioned_user_ids.description: Members to notify (only people who can see the task hear).

tools.name: tasks_session_status
tools.description: Post your session's status on a task you're working on — status, not conversation: state (working · needs_you · ready · failed), a short note, an optional step n of m, links (e.g. a PR), and with ready an optional hand-back summary. It shows as one line on the task, private to the key's person unless they share their agent work; needs_you, ready and failed notify them once. Reporting working after ready or failed starts a new run.

note.description: One line, at most 280 characters (e.g. "Writing tests").

summary.description: The hand-back summary (at most 4,000 characters); its person can post it as a comment.

agent.description: Your name on the line (e.g. "Claude"). Default: the key's name.

tools.name: tasks_reminder_add
tools.description: Remind the key's person about a task: at a time (kind at, with at), or a day or an hour before it's due. Reminders are each person's own; they fire as a notice (and an OS / browser notice where allowed).

tools.name: tasks_reminder_remove
tools.description: Remove one of the key's person's reminders (its id is in tasks_get's my_reminders).

tools.name: tasks_work_session_add
tools.description: Schedule a work session on a task (a block on the calendar): its person is the key's creator, or the task's assignee (person_id). A task can have several.

person_id.description: The task's assignee, when it's their session. Default: the key's creator.

tools.name: tasks_work_session_update
tools.description: Move or resize a work session (its id is in tasks_get's work_sessions); its person stays.

tools.name: tasks_work_session_remove
tools.description: Remove a work session from a task.

tools.name: tasks_skip_occurrence
tools.description: Jump an open recurring task past its pending occurrence without done-credit. Forward-only; the connector computes the next occurrence from the task's rule.

tools.name: tasks_move_occurrence
tools.description: Move just this occurrence of a repeating task ("Move just this one"): a new due date and/or session start; the pattern stays. To change the pattern, send repeat to tasks_update.

due_on.description: This occurrence's due date, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.description: Create a project, owned by the key's creator and seen by the workspace: name, area, status, start and target dates, colour, lead, client (a person or a company; needs Contacts access), description. Inside an import run (import_id) it's recorded for imports_undo. Look for an existing project first (projects_list): a re-run should reuse it.

area_id.description: File it under this area (see areas_list).

status.description: Default active.

color.description: Colour name, as the app's picker has them.

client_contact_id.description: The client, when it's a person: a contact uuid (contacts_search). Not with client_company_id.

client_company_id.description: The client, when it's a company: a company uuid (contacts_search). Not with client_contact_id.

description.description: What the project is, plain text (up to 20,000 characters).

tools.name: projects_update
tools.description: Edit a project you can edit: name, status (active · on_hold · done), area, start and target dates, colour, lead, client (a person or a company; needs Contacts access; setting one clears the other), description, archived (needs full access). Pass only what changes; null clears a date, the area, the lead, the client or the description.

status.description: The project's status.

area_id.description: Area uuid, or null.

client_contact_id.description: The client as a person: a contact uuid (it replaces a company client), or null to clear a person client.

client_company_id.description: The client as a company: a company uuid (it replaces a person client), or null to clear a company client.

description.description: What the project is, plain text (up to 20,000 characters), or null to clear it.

tools.name: projects_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a project you can edit ("Duplicate project…"): its sections, statuses and open tasks, with dates shifted to a new start; nothing done or tracked is copied. Answers with the new project and how many tasks it has.

name.description: The new project's name. Default: the same name.

starts_on.description: The new start date (YYYY-MM-DD); dates shift from it.

area_id.description: File the copy under this area. Default: the source's.

tools.name: sections_create
tools.description: Add a section to a project you can edit (e.g. "Week 1"), with optional start and end dates, after another section or at the end. Inside an import run (import_id) it's recorded for imports_undo. Answers with the project's sections.

ends_on.description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (an end alone is a milestone).

after.description: Put it after this section (null: first). Default: last.

tools.name: areas_create
tools.description: Add an area the sidebar groups projects under (everyone in the workspace sees it).

tools.name: templates_apply
tools.description: Make a task or a project from a template (see templates_list). A task template: optional title, project and section (default: the template's project if you can add tasks there, else your Inbox) and a date its offsets count from. A project template: optional name, start date (dates shift from it) and area.

title.description: Task template: the new task's title.

date.description: Task template: YYYY-MM-DD its dates count from.

name.description: Project template: the new project's name.

area_id.description: Project template: file it under this area.

tools.name: imports_begin
tools.description: Begin an import run ("bring my Todoist / Linear / Trello through your AI"): name the source (e.g. todoist). Pass the run's id as import_id to projects_create, sections_create and tasks_create, give each task imported_from {source, key} with the source's own id, then imports_finish. Running the same import again (a new run) updates the tasks by key and creates nothing new; imports_undo takes a run back.

source.description: Where it comes from, e.g. todoist, linear, trello (at most 40 characters).

label.description: A name for this run, e.g. "Biology syllabus".

tools.name: imports_finish
tools.description: Finish an import run: answers what it made and updated. A finished run takes no more rows.

tools.name: imports_undo
tools.description: Undo an import run ("Undo this import"): what it made and nobody touched since goes to Recently deleted — tasks, then the sections and projects it made that are left empty. Anything edited since stays; rows it only updated stay as they are. Answers the counts.

tools.name: links_search_entities
tools.description: Search the central registry by label — the @mention / link picker source. Excludes tombstones; optionally scoped to entity types.

tools.name: links_list
tools.description: Every live link touching an entity (matched on either end) — the hub roll-up source.

entity_id.description: The focus entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: links_suggest
tools.description: Deterministic auto-suggested links for an entity (shared tags / matching email domain / ±time-window co-activity). Never auto-applied — use links_create to accept.

entity_id.description: The focus entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: comments_list
tools.description: An item's comments (a task's, a note's, …), the newest last: who wrote each (a person by name, an app as "<key name> (app)"), when, whether it was edited, and the text. Read the answers people left you here. Needs View on the item's module too, and shows only what the key's person can open.

entity_id.description: The item's uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: links_create
tools.description: Link two entities with a typed, direction-agnostic relation (idempotent; rejects self-links and unknown kinds). Registers both endpoints.

source_id.description: Source entity uuid (a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142, works too).

target_id.description: Target entity uuid (or a task's handle).

tools.name: links_set_kind
tools.description: Re-type an existing link's relation kind. No-op if unchanged.

tools.name: links_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a link (Undo-friendly, idempotent).

tools.name: comments_add
tools.description: Add a comment to any entity. Member @mentions (mentioned_user_ids) become attributed notifications for those members.

entity_id.description: Commented entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: contacts_list
tools.description: All people and companies in the workspace — the directory source.

tools.name: contacts_get
tools.description: A contact (or company) with every live link touching it — the roll-up hub source.

entity_id.description: The contact/company uuid.

tools.name: contacts_search
tools.description: Search people and companies by name or email.

tools.name: contacts_create
tools.description: Create a person; registers them so they're immediately linkable/@mentionable.

status.description: Flat status label (default lead).

tools.name: contacts_update
tools.description: Edit a person's fields (omit a field to leave it unchanged).

tools.name: contacts_set_status
tools.description: Set a person's flat status (any non-empty label; no pipeline). No-op if unchanged.

status.description: The status label.

tools.name: contacts_link
tools.description: Link a contact/company to another entity (idempotent). Kinds: works-at, follow-up, references, …. A works-at link between a person and a company also makes it the person's company (replacing a previous one); removing it clears that.

target_id.description: Other entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: contacts_unlink
tools.description: Soft-delete a link a contact/company owns (Undo-friendly, idempotent).

tools.name: contacts_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a contact: drops its links and removes it from search / @mention / roll-ups.

tools.name: contacts_import
tools.description: Bulk-create people from a deduped plan: each row { op:'create'|'merge', contactId?, name, email, phone, title, company, status }.

rows.description: The rows to import (each with op='create'|'merge').

tools.name: calendar_list_events
tools.description: Events in a date range — both native Moduo events and mirrored-external ones (read-only, source-attributed). Times are ISO 8601.

tools.name: calendar_day
tools.description: The composed day: native + external events, scheduled task blocks, and the 'unfinished from earlier' strip (open tasks whose scheduled time passed). Pass `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) or omit for today.

date.description: The day to compose (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Defaults to today.

tools.name: calendar_create_event
tools.description: Create a native Moduo event. Times ISO 8601; `rrule` an optional RFC-5545 rule.

description.description: Optional notes.

rrule.description: Optional RFC-5545 RRULE for a repeat.

tools.name: calendar_update_event
tools.description: Edit a native event (only the fields you pass change). External events are rejected.

description.description: New notes.

rrule.description: New RRULE, or empty to clear the repeat.

tools.name: calendar_delete_event
tools.description: Delete a native event (tombstoned; spine links cascade). External events are rejected.

tools.name: calendar_schedule_task
tools.description: Place a task on the calendar at a clock time — it becomes a task block (the lens).

tools.name: calendar_move_block
tools.description: Move an already-scheduled task block to a new time (duration preserved).

tools.name: calendar_complete_block
tools.description: Complete a task from its block (recurrence advances) — same as completing in Tasks.

tools.name: calendar_roll_forward
tools.description: The strip's Move-to-today: reschedule every open task whose scheduled time passed (last 7 days) onto today, preserving each task's clock time. Returns the moved task ids.

tools.name: notes_list
tools.description: The note tree — every live note's id, title, parent, icon, and published flag (trashed excluded). Reconstruct the hierarchy from parent_id.

tools.name: notes_get
tools.description: One note as markdown (`body_md`) plus its meta — the read source.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.description: Full-text search over note titles and body — returns matches with a snippet.

tools.name: notes_create
tools.description: Create a note from markdown (optionally under a parent) — agents build whole trees this way. The note is immediately listable, searchable, publishable and editable, and lands in the Inbox when it has no parent.

title.description: The note title (becomes its first line).

parent_id.description: Parent note uuid to nest under (optional).

tools.name: notes_append
tools.description: Append markdown to the end of a note. It appears live for anyone with the note open, is attributed to this key, and they can undo it.

tools.name: notes_update
tools.description: Replace a note's markdown body wholesale (optionally rename it). It appears live for anyone with the note open, is attributed to this key, and they can undo it.

title.description: New title (optional; also its first line).

tools.name: notes_move
tools.description: Reparent a note (with its subtree) under another note, or to the root (omit parent_id). Cycle-guarded server-side. Ordering among siblings is not controllable here — the note takes a default position.

parent_id.description: New parent uuid, or omit for a root.

tools.name: notes_archive
tools.description: Archive a note (with its subtree) — hides it from the tree, reversible.

tools.name: notes_trash
tools.description: Move a note (with its subtree) to the Trash (soft-delete; 30-day purge, Undo-friendly).

tools.name: notes_link
tools.description: Link a note to another entity with a typed relation (idempotent; rides the spine, so the key also needs Links: Edit). Use `references` for a manual connection.

tools.name: email_list
tools.description: The tissue email threads — the ones deliberately pulled into the workspace (converted / linked / snoozed / followed-up). Metadata only: from, subject, snippet, snooze & follow-up state. Newest first.

tools.name: email_get
tools.description: One tissue thread's metadata by its ref id (never the message body).

tools.name: email_search
tools.description: Search the tissue threads by sender, subject, or snippet (metadata only). Returns matching threads.

tools.name: email_snooze
tools.description: Snooze a thread until a time — it leaves the inbox and returns when due.

tools.name: email_unsnooze
tools.description: Cancel a snooze — the thread returns to the inbox now.

tools.name: email_follow_up
tools.description: Set a follow-up reminder on a thread — notifies at the deadline if no reply arrived.

tools.name: email_clear_follow_up
tools.description: Clear a follow-up reminder on a thread.

tools.name: email_link
tools.description: Link a thread to another entity with a typed relation (idempotent; rides the spine). Use `references` for a manual connection, `spawned-from` when a task came from the thread.

ref_id.description: The email_refs uuid (the thread to link).

target_id.description: Other entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: email_remove
tools.description: Remove a thread from the tissue — soft-deletes the ref, drops its links, tombstones the entity (the inbox itself is untouched; the mailbox is on desktop).

tools.name: chat_list_channels
tools.description: List the conversations this key can read: public channels, and private channels its creator is in when the key's "Include private channels I'm in" is on. Direct messages are never visible to a key.

tools.name: chat_read
tools.description: Read a conversation (its messages, oldest first) or one reply chain when chain_id is given (the chain's first message and its replies). Pages back with before (a message id from the previous page).

channel.description: Conversation name as shown (e.g. Release Train) or id.

chain_id.description: Optional: the first message of a reply chain.

before.description: Optional: read the messages before this message id.

tools.name: chat_search
tools.description: Search messages in the conversations this key can read, newest first. Matches whole words and their beginnings, Polish without diacritics too.

channel.description: Optional: only this conversation (name or id).

tools.name: chat_addressed_to_me
tools.description: What's waiting for the key's creator in Catch up: messages that mention them, their teams or everyone, replies in chains they're in, and announcements, in conversations this key can read (never direct messages). Newest first.

tools.name: chat_post
tools.description: Post a message in a conversation as the key's creator ("Alex · via <key name>"). Write Markdown (**bold**, _italic_, `code`); mention a person with <@USER_ID> and everyone with <!channel> (plain text unless the key's creator may mention everyone). 30 posts a minute per key.

channel.description: Conversation name as shown or id.

thread_id.description: Deprecated: use chat_reply. A message to answer.

tools.name: chat_reply
tools.description: Reply to a message, quoting it: the reply joins that message's chain. Write Markdown (**bold**, _italic_, `code`); mention a person with <@USER_ID> and everyone with <!channel> (plain text unless the key's creator may mention everyone).

tools.name: chat_react
tools.description: Add (or, with on=false, take back) the key creator's reaction on a message: an emoji like 👍, or a workspace emoji as :name:.

on.description: false takes the reaction back (default true).

tools.name: chat_mark_decision
tools.description: Mark a message as a decision (or unmark it with on=false). Decisions show in the conversation's Details and on the items it's linked to.

tools.name: chat_wrap_up
tools.description: Wrap up a reply chain with the reply that settled it (optionally marking that reply as a decision). Whoever started the chain, the channel's managers and admins can.

mark_decision.description: Also mark that reply as a decision.

tools.name: chat_create_channel
tools.description: Create a channel as the key's creator (their role decides whether they may). Private only when the key's "Include private channels I'm in" is on.

name.description: The channel's name, as it should read.

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: The projects the key's person can see, in sidebar order: their Inbox (is_inbox), status (active · on_hold · done), area, colour, start and target dates, lead, client (a person or a company, {type: contact | company, id, name}; only with Contacts access, and only one the person can open), and the project's description (plain text) when it has one. Archived projects (and their tasks) are left out unless include_archived is true; then they carry archived: true.

include_archived.description: Also list archived projects. Default false.

tools.name: tasks_list_buckets
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use projects_list. The workspace's projects ("buckets"; the reserved Inbox is is_system), with area_id and colour. Archived projects (and their tasks) are left out unless include_archived is true; then they carry archived: true.

tools.name: statuses_list
tools.description: A project's statuses, each in its category (backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do), in order; without a project, the workspace's default set (which the Inbox uses). tasks_set_status and tasks_create take a category word, a status's name or its id.

project_id.description: Project uuid. Default: the workspace's default statuses.

tools.name: teams_list
tools.description: The workspace's teams: name, colour, members (with is_me) and their default project when the key's person can see it. tasks_route_team routes a task to one.

tools.name: templates_list

tools.description: Tasks, a short row each (fields: summary, the default): handle, id, title, status (its category; status_name when the project calls it something else), priority, assignee's name (none = Unassigned), project (when the list spans projects), section, tags, due (YYYY-MM-DD, with HH:MM when timed), and blocked, drifted, queued_by_me, subtasks (a count) and parent only when they apply. fields: full gives each task's full shape instead (ids, people, description excerpt, dates, estimate, repeat, …); tasks_get reads one in full. team_id.description: Only tasks routed to this team.

agent_sessions.description: Agent sessions on it the key's person can see.

comments.description: The latest comments, newest last; only with Links: View.

earlier_comments.description: How many older comments comments_list reads.

activity.description: The recent attributed trail, newest first.

tools.name: tasks_history
tools.description: A repeating task's past cycles: when each was done (and by whom) or skipped, newest first.

tools.name: tasks_time_report
tools.description: Tracked time for a period (up to a year), by task or by day, with the total: the key person's own entries, plus teammates' who share their time with the workspace owner when the person is the owner. Only tasks they can see; a project they can't see has no name. Optional: one project.

by.description: Group by task (default) or by day.

tools.name: tasks_attachments_list
tools.description: A task's files (AT-1): name, type, size, when added, and a download link that works for 5 minutes. Links are made for the key's creator; ask again for fresh ones.

tools.name: tasks_activity
tools.description: The attributed intent-op trail (who did what; an agent's rows read "Alex · via <key name>"): one task's trail, or the workspace's most recent activity. Comments aren't in it: read them with comments_list (or tasks_get).

task_id.description: Limit to one task (handle or uuid; optional).

tools.name: tasks_list_assignees
tools.description: Who a task can be assigned to: the workspace's members with is_me for the key's creator. Only people with can_be_assigned (they can work on tasks) are accepted by tasks_assign.

tools.name: tasks_queue_add
tools.description: Add a task to your queue (the key creator's): at the end, or at the top. A task already queued stays where it is unless you ask for the top. Done and archived tasks can't be queued. Returns your queue.

tools.name: tasks_queue_remove
tools.description: Take a task out of your queue. Doing it twice is fine. Returns your queue.

tools.name: tasks_queue_reorder
tools.description: Move a task that's in your queue: to the top, to the end, or right after another task in your queue. Moving never counts as a reschedule. Returns your queue.

task_id.description: Task handle or uuid (must be in your queue).

after_task_id.description: With position 'after': the queued task it should follow.

tools.name: tasks_commit
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use tasks_queue_add. Puts the task at the end of your queue (again: moves it there) and marks it for the day in app versions from before personal queues.

tools.name: tasks_uncommit
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use tasks_queue_remove. Takes the task out of your queue (and off the day in older app versions). Doing it twice is fine.

tools.name: tasks_skip_today
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use tasks_queue_remove. Takes the task out of your queue (and off the day in older app versions). It no longer counts as a reschedule.

tools.name: tasks_create
tools.description: Create a task in one go: filed into a project and section (default: the key creator's Inbox), with a status (a category word, the project's status name or id), assignee (a member, "me", or null; default the key's creator), team, due date and time, estimate, priority, tags (by name; new ones are made and coloured as the app colours them), a repeat (RRULE), reminders, work sessions and a parent (one level). With imported_from {source, key} it remembers where it came from; sending a key you already used on a live task of yours updates that task instead (a re-run). Inside an import run (import_id), it is recorded for imports_undo. Nothing is written if any part is refused. It gets its handle (e.g. MOD-142), shows in search at once, and the trail reads "<person> · via <key name>".

project_id.description: Project uuid (see projects_list). Default: the key creator's Inbox.

section_id.description: Section uuid in that project (see sections_list).

parent_id.description: Make it a subtask of this task (handle or uuid; one level only).

description.description: Longer notes. Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ``` fenced code ```, [links](https://…), "- " bullets, "1. " numbers, "- [ ] " checkboxes, "> " quotes (HTML is converted). Reference an item as [task](moduo://task/<uuid or handle, e.g. MOD-12>) (or note, contact, company, email_thread, event, project; it shows by name to whoever can open it, an item you cannot reach stays as its words, and with Links at Edit each one is linked from the task), a date as [Oct 17](moduo://date/2026-10-17).

status.description: backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do, or the project's status name or id. Default: to do.

assignee_id.description: Member uuid (see tasks_list_assignees), "me", or null for Unassigned.

team_id.description: Route it to this team (see teams_list); nobody's until someone takes it.

due_on.description: Due date, YYYY-MM-DD (the same date for everyone).

due_date.description: Older due field: a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO 8601.

scheduled_at.description: Older field: when to work on it, ISO 8601 (prefer sessions).

repeat.description: An RRULE like FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU, or {rrule, mode: "after_completion"}.

reminders.description: Your reminders: {kind: at | day_before | hour_before, at?: ISO 8601 (for at)}; at most 10.

sessions.description: Work sessions: {starts_at, ends_at} (ISO 8601); yours, at most 10.

imported_from.description: {source, key}: where an import brought it from (e.g. {source: "linear", key: "ENG-123"}).

import_id.description: The run from imports_begin, so imports_undo can take it back.

tools.name: tasks_update
tools.description: Edit a task's fields: title, description, project (its subtasks you can edit move with it), section, parent, status (category word or the project's name), team, due date and time, estimate, priority, energy, repeat (null stops it), and tags (tags_add / tags_remove by name). Pass only what changes; null clears. The assignee has its own tool (tasks_assign).

section_id.description: Section uuid in its project, or null.

parent_id.description: Parent task (handle or uuid), or null for top level.

description.description: New description (replaces it whole). Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ``` fenced code ```, [links](https://…), "- " bullets, "1. " numbers, "- [ ] " checkboxes, "> " quotes (HTML is converted). Reference an item as [task](moduo://task/<uuid or handle, e.g. MOD-12>) (or note, contact, company, email_thread, event, project; it shows by name to whoever can open it, an item you cannot reach stays as its words, and with Links at Edit each one is linked from the task), a date as [Oct 17](moduo://date/2026-10-17).

status.description: A category word, or the project's status name or id.

team_id.description: Team uuid, or null.

due_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear.

due_date.description: Older due field: a date or ISO 8601, or null.

scheduled_at.description: Older field: ISO 8601, or null to clear.

repeat.description: An RRULE or {rrule, mode}; null stops the repeat.

tools.name: tasks_set_status
tools.description: Change a task's status: a category word (backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do; the older archived = won't do), or the project's own status name (any case) or id; see statuses_list. Finishing a task finishes its open subtasks you can edit too (also_finished counts them); a repeat moves to its next occurrence instead (the server keeps the pointer; missed occurrences don't exist).

status.description: Category word, status name or status id.

tools.name: tasks_reschedule
tools.description: Move a scheduled task's time (drift triage). Does not touch the reschedule counter.

tools.name: tasks_unschedule
tools.description: Clear a task's stale scheduled time, keeping the task (drift-triage Ignore).

tools.name: tasks_assign
tools.description: Assign a task to a member who can work on tasks, or unassign it with null. "me" is the key's creator. Someone else being assigned gets one "assigned to you" notification; an unfiled task given to someone goes into their Inbox.

assignee_id.description: Member uuid (see tasks_list_assignees), "me", or null to unassign.

tools.name: tasks_route_team
tools.description: Route a task to a team (see teams_list), or take it off its team with null. Routing doesn't unassign: to hand your own task to a team, unassign it too. A task in an Inbox goes to the team's default project.

team_id.description: Team uuid, or null.

tools.name: tasks_claim
tools.description: Take a task routed to one of your teams: it becomes the key creator's. Needs edit access to it; "Someone already took this task." when another member was first.

tools.name: tasks_handoff
tools.description: Hand a task off: it now waits on a member (person_id) or on what you name (label, e.g. "the client's sign-off"). The assignee stays; the entry clears itself when that person comments. tasks_waiting_clear removes one.

label.description: Or what it waits on, in words (at most 200 characters).

tools.name: tasks_waiting_clear
tools.description: Remove one "waiting on" entry from a task (its id is in tasks_get's waiting_on).

tools.name: tasks_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a task — only when a person asked you to (your own changes are already in the trail). It reads as written by this key's app. Needs Links: Edit too.

mentioned_user_ids.description: Members to notify (only people who can see the task hear).

tools.name: tasks_session_status
tools.description: Post your session's status on a task you're working on — status, not conversation: state (working · needs_you · ready · failed), a short note, an optional step n of m, links (e.g. a PR), and with ready an optional hand-back summary. It shows as one line on the task, private to the key's person unless they share their agent work; needs_you, ready and failed notify them once. Reporting working after ready or failed starts a new run.

note.description: One line, at most 280 characters (e.g. "Writing tests").

summary.description: The hand-back summary (at most 4,000 characters); its person can post it as a comment.

agent.description: Your name on the line (e.g. "Claude"). Default: the key's name.

tools.name: tasks_reminder_add
tools.description: Remind the key's person about a task: at a time (kind at, with at), or a day or an hour before it's due. Reminders are each person's own; they fire as a notice (and an OS / browser notice where allowed).

tools.name: tasks_reminder_remove
tools.description: Remove one of the key's person's reminders (its id is in tasks_get's my_reminders).

tools.name: tasks_work_session_add
tools.description: Schedule a work session on a task (a block on the calendar): its person is the key's creator, or the task's assignee (person_id). A task can have several.

person_id.description: The task's assignee, when it's their session. Default: the key's creator.

tools.name: tasks_work_session_update
tools.description: Move or resize a work session (its id is in tasks_get's work_sessions); its person stays.

tools.name: tasks_work_session_remove
tools.description: Remove a work session from a task.

tools.name: tasks_skip_occurrence
tools.description: Jump an open recurring task past its pending occurrence without done-credit. Forward-only; the connector computes the next occurrence from the task's rule.

tools.name: tasks_move_occurrence
tools.description: Move just this occurrence of a repeating task ("Move just this one"): a new due date and/or session start; the pattern stays. To change the pattern, send repeat to tasks_update.

due_on.description: This occurrence's due date, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: projects_create
tools.description: Create a project, owned by the key's creator and seen by the workspace: name, area, status, start and target dates, colour, lead, client (a person or a company; needs Contacts access), description. Inside an import run (import_id) it's recorded for imports_undo. Look for an existing project first (projects_list): a re-run should reuse it.

area_id.description: File it under this area (see areas_list).

status.description: Default active.

color.description: Colour name, as the app's picker has them.

client_contact_id.description: The client, when it's a person: a contact uuid (contacts_search). Not with client_company_id.

client_company_id.description: The client, when it's a company: a company uuid (contacts_search). Not with client_contact_id.

description.description: What the project is, plain text (up to 20,000 characters).

tools.name: projects_update
tools.description: Edit a project you can edit: name, status (active · on_hold · done), area, start and target dates, colour, lead, client (a person or a company; needs Contacts access; setting one clears the other), description, archived (needs full access). Pass only what changes; null clears a date, the area, the lead, the client or the description.

status.description: The project's status.

area_id.description: Area uuid, or null.

client_contact_id.description: The client as a person: a contact uuid (it replaces a company client), or null to clear a person client.

client_company_id.description: The client as a company: a company uuid (it replaces a person client), or null to clear a company client.

description.description: What the project is, plain text (up to 20,000 characters), or null to clear it.

tools.name: projects_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a project you can edit ("Duplicate project…"): its sections, statuses and open tasks, with dates shifted to a new start; nothing done or tracked is copied. Answers with the new project and how many tasks it has.

name.description: The new project's name. Default: the same name.

starts_on.description: The new start date (YYYY-MM-DD); dates shift from it.

area_id.description: File the copy under this area. Default: the source's.

tools.name: sections_create
tools.description: Add a section to a project you can edit (e.g. "Week 1"), with optional start and end dates, after another section or at the end. Inside an import run (import_id) it's recorded for imports_undo. Answers with the project's sections.

ends_on.description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (an end alone is a milestone).

after.description: Put it after this section (null: first). Default: last.

tools.name: areas_create
tools.description: Add an area the sidebar groups projects under (everyone in the workspace sees it).

tools.name: templates_apply
tools.description: Make a task or a project from a template (see templates_list). A task template: optional title, project and section (default: the template's project if you can add tasks there, else your Inbox) and a date its offsets count from. A project template: optional name, start date (dates shift from it) and area.

title.description: Task template: the new task's title.

date.description: Task template: YYYY-MM-DD its dates count from.

name.description: Project template: the new project's name.

area_id.description: Project template: file it under this area.

tools.name: imports_begin
tools.description: Begin an import run ("bring my Todoist / Linear / Trello through your AI"): name the source (e.g. todoist). Pass the run's id as import_id to projects_create, sections_create and tasks_create, give each task imported_from {source, key} with the source's own id, then imports_finish. Running the same import again (a new run) updates the tasks by key and creates nothing new; imports_undo takes a run back.

source.description: Where it comes from, e.g. todoist, linear, trello (at most 40 characters).

label.description: A name for this run, e.g. "Biology syllabus".

tools.name: imports_finish
tools.description: Finish an import run: answers what it made and updated. A finished run takes no more rows.

tools.name: imports_undo
tools.description: Undo an import run ("Undo this import"): what it made and nobody touched since goes to Recently deleted — tasks, then the sections and projects it made that are left empty. Anything edited since stays; rows it only updated stay as they are. Answers the counts.

tools.name: links_search_entities
tools.description: Search the central registry by label — the @mention / link picker source. Excludes tombstones; optionally scoped to entity types.

tools.name: links_list
tools.description: Every live link touching an entity (matched on either end) — the hub roll-up source.

entity_id.description: The focus entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: links_suggest
tools.description: Deterministic auto-suggested links for an entity (shared tags / matching email domain / ±time-window co-activity). Never auto-applied — use links_create to accept.

entity_id.description: The focus entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: comments_list
tools.description: An item's comments (a task's, a note's, …), the newest last: who wrote each (a person by name, an app as "<key name> (app)"), when, whether it was edited, and the text. Read the answers people left you here. Needs View on the item's module too, and shows only what the key's person can open.

entity_id.description: The item's uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: links_create
tools.description: Link two entities with a typed, direction-agnostic relation (idempotent; rejects self-links and unknown kinds). Registers both endpoints.

source_id.description: Source entity uuid (a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142, works too).

target_id.description: Target entity uuid (or a task's handle).

tools.name: links_set_kind
tools.description: Re-type an existing link's relation kind. No-op if unchanged.

tools.name: links_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a link (Undo-friendly, idempotent).

tools.name: comments_add
tools.description: Add a comment to any entity. Member @mentions (mentioned_user_ids) become attributed notifications for those members.

entity_id.description: Commented entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: contacts_list
tools.description: All people and companies in the workspace — the directory source.

tools.name: contacts_get
tools.description: A contact (or company) with every live link touching it — the roll-up hub source.

entity_id.description: The contact/company uuid.

tools.name: contacts_search
tools.description: Search people and companies by name or email.

tools.name: contacts_create
tools.description: Create a person; registers them so they're immediately linkable/@mentionable.

status.description: Flat status label (default lead).

tools.name: contacts_update
tools.description: Edit a person's fields (omit a field to leave it unchanged).

tools.name: contacts_set_status
tools.description: Set a person's flat status (any non-empty label; no pipeline). No-op if unchanged.

status.description: The status label.

tools.name: contacts_link
tools.description: Link a contact/company to another entity (idempotent). Kinds: works-at, follow-up, references, …. A works-at link between a person and a company also makes it the person's company (replacing a previous one); removing it clears that.

target_id.description: Other entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: contacts_unlink
tools.description: Soft-delete a link a contact/company owns (Undo-friendly, idempotent).

tools.name: contacts_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a contact: drops its links and removes it from search / @mention / roll-ups.

tools.name: contacts_import
tools.description: Bulk-create people from a deduped plan: each row { op:'create'|'merge', contactId?, name, email, phone, title, company, status }.

rows.description: The rows to import (each with op='create'|'merge').

tools.name: calendar_list_events
tools.description: Events in a date range — both native Moduo events and mirrored-external ones (read-only, source-attributed). Times are ISO 8601.

tools.name: calendar_day
tools.description: The composed day: native + external events, scheduled task blocks, and the 'unfinished from earlier' strip (open tasks whose scheduled time passed). Pass `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) or omit for today.

date.description: The day to compose (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Defaults to today.

tools.name: calendar_create_event
tools.description: Create a native Moduo event. Times ISO 8601; `rrule` an optional RFC-5545 rule.

description.description: Optional notes.

rrule.description: Optional RFC-5545 RRULE for a repeat.

tools.name: calendar_update_event
tools.description: Edit a native event (only the fields you pass change). External events are rejected.

description.description: New notes.

rrule.description: New RRULE, or empty to clear the repeat.

tools.name: calendar_delete_event
tools.description: Delete a native event (tombstoned; spine links cascade). External events are rejected.

tools.name: calendar_schedule_task
tools.description: Place a task on the calendar at a clock time — it becomes a task block (the lens).

tools.name: calendar_move_block
tools.description: Move an already-scheduled task block to a new time (duration preserved).

tools.name: calendar_complete_block
tools.description: Complete a task from its block (recurrence advances) — same as completing in Tasks.

tools.name: calendar_roll_forward
tools.description: The strip's Move-to-today: reschedule every open task whose scheduled time passed (last 7 days) onto today, preserving each task's clock time. Returns the moved task ids.

tools.name: notes_list
tools.description: The note tree — every live note's id, title, parent, icon, and published flag (trashed excluded). Reconstruct the hierarchy from parent_id.

tools.name: notes_get
tools.description: One note as markdown (`body_md`) plus its meta — the read source.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.description: Full-text search over note titles and body — returns matches with a snippet.

tools.name: notes_create
tools.description: Create a note from markdown (optionally under a parent) — agents build whole trees this way. The note is immediately listable, searchable, publishable and editable, and lands in the Inbox when it has no parent.

title.description: The note title (becomes its first line).

parent_id.description: Parent note uuid to nest under (optional).

tools.name: notes_append
tools.description: Append markdown to the end of a note. It appears live for anyone with the note open, is attributed to this key, and they can undo it.

tools.name: notes_update
tools.description: Replace a note's markdown body wholesale (optionally rename it). It appears live for anyone with the note open, is attributed to this key, and they can undo it.

title.description: New title (optional; also its first line).

tools.name: notes_move
tools.description: Reparent a note (with its subtree) under another note, or to the root (omit parent_id). Cycle-guarded server-side. Ordering among siblings is not controllable here — the note takes a default position.

parent_id.description: New parent uuid, or omit for a root.

tools.name: notes_archive
tools.description: Archive a note (with its subtree) — hides it from the tree, reversible.

tools.name: notes_trash
tools.description: Move a note (with its subtree) to the Trash (soft-delete; 30-day purge, Undo-friendly).

tools.name: notes_link
tools.description: Link a note to another entity with a typed relation (idempotent; rides the spine, so the key also needs Links: Edit). Use `references` for a manual connection.

tools.name: email_list
tools.description: The tissue email threads — the ones deliberately pulled into the workspace (converted / linked / snoozed / followed-up). Metadata only: from, subject, snippet, snooze & follow-up state. Newest first.

tools.name: email_get
tools.description: One tissue thread's metadata by its ref id (never the message body).

tools.name: email_search
tools.description: Search the tissue threads by sender, subject, or snippet (metadata only). Returns matching threads.

tools.name: email_snooze
tools.description: Snooze a thread until a time — it leaves the inbox and returns when due.

tools.name: email_unsnooze
tools.description: Cancel a snooze — the thread returns to the inbox now.

tools.name: email_follow_up
tools.description: Set a follow-up reminder on a thread — notifies at the deadline if no reply arrived.

tools.name: email_clear_follow_up
tools.description: Clear a follow-up reminder on a thread.

tools.name: email_link
tools.description: Link a thread to another entity with a typed relation (idempotent; rides the spine). Use `references` for a manual connection, `spawned-from` when a task came from the thread.

ref_id.description: The email_refs uuid (the thread to link).

target_id.description: Other entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: email_remove
tools.description: Remove a thread from the tissue — soft-deletes the ref, drops its links, tombstones the entity (the inbox itself is untouched; the mailbox is on desktop).

tools.name: chat_list_channels
tools.description: List the conversations this key can read: public channels, and private channels its creator is in when the key's "Include private channels I'm in" is on. Direct messages are never visible to a key.

tools.name: chat_read
tools.description: Read a conversation (its messages, oldest first) or one reply chain when chain_id is given (the chain's first message and its replies). Pages back with before (a message id from the previous page).

channel.description: Conversation name as shown (e.g. Release Train) or id.

chain_id.description: Optional: the first message of a reply chain.

before.description: Optional: read the messages before this message id.

tools.name: chat_search
tools.description: Search messages in the conversations this key can read, newest first. Matches whole words and their beginnings, Polish without diacritics too.

channel.description: Optional: only this conversation (name or id).

tools.name: chat_addressed_to_me
tools.description: What's waiting for the key's creator in Catch up: messages that mention them, their teams or everyone, replies in chains they're in, and announcements, in conversations this key can read (never direct messages). Newest first.

tools.name: chat_post
tools.description: Post a message in a conversation as the key's creator ("Alex · via <key name>"). Write Markdown (**bold**, _italic_, `code`); mention a person with <@USER_ID> and everyone with <!channel> (plain text unless the key's creator may mention everyone). 30 posts a minute per key.

channel.description: Conversation name as shown or id.

thread_id.description: Deprecated: use chat_reply. A message to answer.

tools.name: chat_reply
tools.description: Reply to a message, quoting it: the reply joins that message's chain. Write Markdown (**bold**, _italic_, `code`); mention a person with <@USER_ID> and everyone with <!channel> (plain text unless the key's creator may mention everyone).

tools.name: chat_react
tools.description: Add (or, with on=false, take back) the key creator's reaction on a message: an emoji like 👍, or a workspace emoji as :name:.

on.description: false takes the reaction back (default true).

tools.name: chat_mark_decision
tools.description: Mark a message as a decision (or unmark it with on=false). Decisions show in the conversation's Details and on the items it's linked to.

tools.name: chat_wrap_up
tools.description: Wrap up a reply chain with the reply that settled it (optionally marking that reply as a decision). Whoever started the chain, the channel's managers and admins can.

mark_decision.description: Also mark that reply as a decision.

tools.name: chat_create_channel
tools.description: Create a channel as the key's creator (their role decides whether they may). Private only when the key's "Include private channels I'm in" is on.

name.description: The channel's name, as it should read.

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: The projects the key's person can see, in sidebar order: their Inbox (is_inbox), status (active · on_hold · done), area, colour, start and target dates, lead, client (a person or a company, {type: contact | company, id, name}; only with Contacts access, and only one the person can open), and the project's description (plain text) when it has one. Archived projects (and their tasks) are left out unless include_archived is true; then they carry archived: true.

include_archived.description: Also list archived projects. Default false.

tools.name: tasks_list_buckets
tools.description: Deprecated (kept until TV-D7): use projects_list. The workspace's projects ("buckets"; the reserved Inbox is is_system), with area_id and colour. Archived projects (and their tasks) are left out unless include_archived is true; then they carry archived: true.

include_archived.description: Also list archived projects, marked archived: true. Default false.

tools.name: areas_list
tools.description: The areas the sidebar groups projects under, as the key's person sees them.

tools.name: sections_list
tools.description: A project's sections, in order, with their optional start and end dates (an end alone is a milestone).

tools.name: statuses_list
tools.description: A project's statuses, each in its category (backlog · todo · in_progress · done · wont_do), in order; without a project, the workspace's default set (which the Inbox uses). tasks_set_status and tasks_create take a category word, a status's name or its id.

project_id.description: Project uuid. Default: the workspace's default statuses.

tools.name: teams_list
tools.description: The workspace's teams: name, colour, members (with is_me) and their default project when the key's person can see it. tasks_route_team routes a task to one.

tools.name: templates_list

tools.name: email_unsnooze

target_id.description: Other entity uuid (or a task's handle, e.g. MOD-142).

tools.name: email_remove
tools.description: Remove a thread from the tissue — soft-deletes the ref, drops its links, tombstones the entity (the inbox itself is untouched; the mailbox is on desktop).

tools.name: chat_list_channels
tools.description: List the conversations this key can read: public channels, and private channels its creator is in when the key's "Include private channels I'm in" is on. Direct messages are never visible to a key.

tools.name: chat_read
tools.description: Read a conversation (its messages, oldest first) or one reply chain when chain_id is given (the chain's first message and its replies). Pages back with before (a message id from the previous page).

channel.description: Conversation name as shown (e.g. Release Train) or id.

chain_id.description: Optional: the first message of a reply chain.

before.description: Optional: read the messages before this message id.

tools.name: chat_search
tools.description: Search messages in the conversations this key can read, newest first. Matches whole words and their beginnings, Polish without diacritics too.

channel.description: Optional: only this conversation (name or id).

tools.description: Mark a message as a decision (or unmark it with on=false). Decisions show in the conversation's Details and on the items it's linked to.

tools.name: chat_wrap_up
tools.description: Wrap up a reply chain with the reply that settled it (optionally marking that reply as a decision). Whoever started the chain, the channel's managers and admins can.

mark_decision.description: Also mark that reply as a decision.

name.description: The channel's name, as it should read.
